DOCUMENT:
Vendor Comparison: Standard Parcel Delivery Contract
Larkspur Home, Operations, June 2026

1. Purpose
Our contract with our current standard-delivery carrier ends on 30 September 2026. This paper compares three shortlisted carriers and recommends which should carry our standard (two-to-four-day) parcels from October.

2. Volumes and requirements
We dispatch an average of 42,000 standard parcels a month: about 70% weigh under 2 kg (cushions, textiles, small homeware) and 30% weigh 2 to 10 kg (lamps, mirrors, small furniture). Our requirements are on-time delivery of at least 95%, a damage rate below 0.5%, full tracking, and a returns service.

Damage and loss matter to us commercially. Each damaged or lost parcel costs us on average £48 in replacement stock, return shipping and customer service time, and damaged items are the most common cause of one-star reviews.

3. Trial
Between 1 April and 31 May 2026, each shortlisted carrier delivered a share of our orders, allocated at random by the warehouse management system, about 5,000 parcels per carrier. We measured on-time delivery against the promised date, damage reported by customers within 14 days, and lost parcels.

Table 1. Prices and trial performance
Carrier | Price, under 2 kg | Price, 2-10 kg | On-time delivery | Damage rate | Lost per 10,000 parcels
SwiftDrop | £3.10 | £4.60 | 96.2% | 0.4% | 3
ParcelLine | £2.85 | £4.95 | 93.1% | 0.9% | 8
Meridian | £3.30 | £4.40 | 97.5% | 0.3% | 2

On-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers during the trial, and all three offer full tracking and a returns service.

4. Cost comparison
Applying our 70/30 weight mix, the average cost per parcel is £3.55 for SwiftDrop, £3.48 for ParcelLine and £3.63 for Meridian. On 42,000 parcels a month, the monthly cost would be £149,100 for SwiftDrop, £146,160 for ParcelLine and £152,460 for Meridian. ParcelLine is therefore the cheapest option, saving £2,940 a month against SwiftDrop and £6,300 a month against Meridian, or between about £35,000 and £76,000 a year.

5. Customer contact
"Where is my order?" contacts are our largest single category of customer service enquiry. During the trial, ParcelLine deliveries generated 6 such contacts per 1,000 parcels, compared with 11 for SwiftDrop and 10 for Meridian. ParcelLine's live-tracking app clearly reduces customer contacts, and at an average handling cost of £3.20 per contact this would save about £670 a month at our volumes. From 1 May, ParcelLine parcels also carried our new proactive delivery-day text message, which we were testing on one carrier before rolling it out.

6. Other considerations
All three carriers can collect from our warehouse daily at 6 pm. ParcelLine and SwiftDrop offer a 12-month contract; Meridian requires 24 months. SwiftDrop and Meridian have both handled our peak-season volumes for other retailers of similar size, while ParcelLine's references were mainly from fashion retailers with lighter parcels.

All three carriers integrate with our warehouse management system through standard interfaces, and none would require changes to our packing process or labelling. Each offers recipients a delivery-preference service to nominate a safe place or a neighbour, and each provides proof-of-delivery photographs, which our customer service team has found useful in resolving disputes.

7. Recommendation
ParcelLine offers the lowest delivery cost, met our service requirements in the trial and reduces customer contacts through its tracking app. We recommend awarding the standard parcel contract to ParcelLine for 12 months from 1 October 2026, saving up to £76,000 a year against the alternatives.

KEY (three known flaws):
1. [misread_evidence] at: "On-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers during the trial" -- Table 1 shows ParcelLine's on-time delivery was 93.1%, below the 95% requirement. The claim (and the recommendation that ParcelLine 'met our service requirements') misreads the table; ParcelLine's 0.9% damage rate also fails the stated 0.5% requirement.
2. [unsupported_causal] at: "ParcelLine's live-tracking app clearly reduces customer contacts" -- The document states that from 1 May ParcelLine parcels alone also carried the new proactive delivery-day text message. That concurrent intervention confounds the comparison, so the lower contact rate cannot be attributed to ParcelLine's tracking app.
3. [missing_consideration] at: "ParcelLine is therefore the cheapest option, saving £2,940 a month against SwiftDrop" -- The cost comparison ignores the stated £48 cost of each damaged or lost parcel. ParcelLine's damage and loss rates (0.9% and 8 per 10,000) versus SwiftDrop's (0.4% and 3 per 10,000) imply about 231 extra problem parcels a month (about £11,100), far exceeding the £2,940 price saving; ParcelLine is likely the most expensive option overall.

REVIEW:
This paper recommends ParcelLine for the standard parcel contract from October. It rests on three claims: ParcelLine is cheapest at the 70/30 weight mix; all three carriers met the 95% on-time requirement in a randomised trial; and ParcelLine's tracking app roughly halves "where is my order?" contacts.

Several parts are sound:
- **The trial design.** Random allocation of about 5,000 parcels per carrier is a strong design for a head-to-head comparison.
- **The cost arithmetic.** The weighted prices (£3.55, £3.48, £3.63), monthly costs and savings are all correct.
- **The cost of damage.** The paper establishes that damage costs about £48 per incident.

However, the trial results show ParcelLine failing both of the paper's own service requirements. Once its higher damage rate is costed at the paper's own £48, ParcelLine becomes the most expensive option, not the cheapest.

## 1. ParcelLine failed two of the four requirements

| Requirement (Section 2) | SwiftDrop | ParcelLine | Meridian |
|---|---|---|---|
| On-time ≥ 95% | 96.2% ✅ | **93.1% ❌** | 97.5% ✅ |
| Damage < 0.5% | 0.4% ✅ | **0.9% ❌** | 0.3% ✅ |

The statement that "on-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers" contradicts Table 1. The same claim appears in the recommendation and in the author's note. The paper never compares the damage rates with the 0.5% threshold.

## 2. ParcelLine is the most expensive once damage and loss are costed

Using the paper's own figure of £48 per damaged or lost parcel, at 42,000 parcels a month:

| | SwiftDrop | ParcelLine | Meridian |
|---|---|---|---|
| Delivery cost | £149,100 | £146,160 | £152,460 |
| Damaged + lost parcels | ~181 | ~412 | ~134 |
| Damage and loss cost (× £48) | £8,670 | £19,760 | £6,450 |
| **Total per month** | **£157,770** | **£165,920** | **£158,910** |

ParcelLine costs about **£8,150 a month more than SwiftDrop** and **£7,000 more than Meridian**. That is roughly **£84,000–£98,000 a year**, the reverse of the claimed saving of up to £76,000. The damage gap alone outweighs the price advantage: ParcelLine damages about 231 more parcels a month than SwiftDrop, which costs around £11,000 against a price saving of £2,940.

This still understates the gap. The £48 figure doesn't include the cost of one-star reviews, which the paper identifies as mainly driven by damage.

## 3. The drop in customer contacts may come from the text message, not the app

From 1 May, half-way through the trial, ParcelLine parcels alone carried the new delivery-day text. The trial therefore can't separate the effect of the app from the effect of the text. Two other observations point toward the text:
- **The text is the likelier cause.** Proactive notification is a common way to cut "where is my order?" contacts.
- **Lateness didn't push contacts up.** ParcelLine had the *most* late parcels, about 2,900 a month at 93.1%, yet the fewest contacts. Late parcels normally generate them.

The text is being rolled out to all carriers, so any advantage it gave ParcelLine will disappear. Even taken at face value, the £670 a month saving is small next to the damage costs above.

The trial data should show whether ParcelLine's contact rate fell after 1 May. If it did, the app's own effect is smaller than claimed.

## 4. The trial's limits

- **Lost-parcel figures rest on very small numbers.** At about 5,000 parcels each, the rates mean roughly 1, 1.5 and 4 parcels. A rate of 3 per 10,000 implies 1.5 parcels, which suggests the sample sizes weren't exactly 5,000. These figures don't support firm comparisons. The damage rates (about 15–45 incidents each) are a firmer basis.
- **April and May are not peak season.** The paper also notes that ParcelLine's references are mainly from retailers with lighter parcels. The 30% of parcels weighing 2–10 kg, such as lamps and mirrors, are the ones most at risk. ParcelLine's damage rate broken down by weight band would be valuable here.

## 5. Options the paper doesn't consider

**SwiftDrop alone** is the cheapest option once damage is included, by about £1,100 a month over Meridian. It meets every requirement and offers a 12-month term.

**Meridian** has the best service, with the highest on-time rate and the lowest damage and loss. It has peak-season references for similar retailers. It costs only slightly more than SwiftDrop, but requires a 24-month term.

**A split by weight** is worth costing. Meridian is cheapest for 2–10 kg parcels and SwiftDrop is good value under 2 kg. A split would cost about **£3.49 per parcel (£146,580 a month)**, almost exactly ParcelLine's headline price, but with two carriers that meet the requirements. Running two carriers adds operational complexity, so the saving needs weighing against it. The damage rates would also need checking by weight band.

## On the author's description

| Claim | What the document shows |
|---|---|
| "All three carriers cleared our 95% on-time threshold" | ParcelLine: 93.1% |
| "Not trading reliability for price" | ParcelLine fails both on-time and damage requirements |
| "Saving between about £35,000 and £76,000 a year" | True for delivery prices alone. With damage costed, ParcelLine costs about £84,000–£98,000 a year *more* |
| Fewer contacts "shows the value of its live-tracking app" | ParcelLine alone also carried the new delivery-day text from 1 May |
| Randomised, fair head-to-head | True, and a real strength of the paper |

## Recommendation

The trial supports **not** awarding the contract to ParcelLine. On the paper's own requirements and costs:
1. **SwiftDrop** is the best value on a 12-month term.
2. **Meridian** is the stronger choice if peak-season reliability and review risk are weighted heavily enough to justify the longer term.
3. **A SwiftDrop/Meridian split by weight** deserves a quick costing.

Before deciding, revise the paper to cost damage and loss for each carrier, compare each carrier against all four requirements, split the contact data before and after 1 May, and report damage rates by weight band.
